Accounts with an active loan have about twice the chance of falling below 6 months of runway after a 55% income shock.

This is an association within the supplied historical data, not proof that loans cause vulnerability.

DISCOVERY 01 / AN INCOME PARADOX

Higher inflows don't always mean a bigger safety net

The highest income quartile in this historical sample has fewer months of normal spending saved. Pension-majority accounts are excluded.

Money in includes transfers. Correlation is not causation.

DISCOVERY 02 / BALANCE WARNING

Below zero deserves attention

Observed balance dips and the challenge's debt status might be definitionally related. Small samples cannot support a predictive claim.

DISCOVERY 03 / THE EI CLIFF

An illustrative zero income after six months, not an actual EI benefits determination.

Method: monthly income and spending are account medians. Buffer is the average daily balance over the latest six account months. Income is reduced to 55% and other spending remains unchanged. Results describe this modeled shock only. Historic bank transfers and pensions can be included in “money in”.

06 / TRANSPARENT MATH

How every number works.

The benchmark definitions from Tangerine's README, with the assumptions exposed.

Typical monthly money in (I)

Median of `money_in` across all months for the account.

Typical monthly spending (S)

Median of `money_out` across all months for the account.

Typical fixed costs (F)

Median of the monthly sum of `household_bills + insurance + loan_payments`.

Buffer (B)

Mean `avg_daily_balance` for the last six monthly rows, sorted by month.

Household bills (H)

Median of `household_bills`. Percentage increases apply to H.

Active loan payment (P)

`monthly_payment` in `loans.csv` for status C or D at the end of 2025, otherwise zero. Shown separately and not added again to spending.

Runway

First subtract one time costs from B. Let monthly gap = shocked spending − shocked income. If buffer left ≤ 0, runway = 0. If gap ≤ 0, show “no shortfall (120+)”. Otherwise, show the smaller of buffer left ÷ gap and 120, to one decimal.

Source: PKDD'99 Discovery Challenge Financial dataset via the CTU Prague Relational Dataset Repository. Dates and amounts follow the challenge's transformed CSV files. The original regions are not Canadian. No client identifiers or banking information are sent to any third party by this dashboard.
